privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.tldr: The short version: I store as little data as possible, webhook URLs are encrypted, logs delete themselves after 30 days, and you can wipe everything anytime. Nothing is sold, nothing is shared with anyone.
privacy.s1d: Only what's needed to run the app: Discord ID, username, avatar, webhook URLs (encrypted), message templates, and delivery logs. That's it — no other data collected quietly in the background.
privacy.s2d: A webhook URL is direct access to your Discord server, so it's guarded seriously: encrypted with AES-256-GCM before it ever touches the database. The plaintext never reaches the browser, never lands in logs or error trackers. Even if the database leaks, all anyone gets is useless ciphertext.
privacy.s3d: Delivery logs are deleted automatically after 30 days — no request needed. Want a full wipe right now? Settings → Delete Account removes all your data permanently.
privacy.s4d: I don't read, moderate, or snoop on your messages — none of my business. Content is only stored in logs if you personally enable "Save message payload".
privacy.s5d: Just a session cookie for login (HttpOnly, Secure). No ad trackers, no third-party analytics following you around.
privacy.s6d: Want to export your data? You can. Delete everything? Anytime, no drama. Something looks off or you have questions? Contact me directly.

docs.title: API Documentation
docs.intro: My-Kait exposes a small REST API so your own scripts and bots can send messages through your webhooks. Everything the API can do, you can already do in the dashboard — a key never grants more power than your own account.
docs.authBody: Every request must carry your API key in the Authorization header:
docs.authNote: Create keys in Settings → API Keys. The full key is shown exactly once — only its SHA-256 hash is stored, so a leaked database reveals nothing usable. Revoke a key any time; it stops working immediately.
docs.pWebhookIdD: string · ID of one of your saved webhooks. The webhook must belong to you.
docs.pManualUrlD: string · A raw Discord webhook URL. Exactly one of webhookId / manualUrl is required.
docs.pPayloadD: object · required · The Discord message — content (max 2000 chars), username, avatar_url, embeds, … Same shape as the dashboard editor.
docs.pSavePayloadD: boolean · Store the payload in your logs. Default true.
docs.pIdemD: string · Your own unique key per send. Retrying with the same key returns the original result instead of sending twice.
docs.exampleCurl:
curl -X POST https://my-kait.vercel.app/api/v1/send \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer mk_live_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "webhookId": "your-webhook-id",
    "payload": { "content": "Hello from the API" },
    "mode": "normal"
  }'
docs.e401: 401 · missing_api_key, invalid_api_key, api_key_revoked, api_key_expired — bad, revoked, or expired key.
docs.e403: 403 · insufficient_scope — the key lacks the required scope.
docs.e400: 400 · invalid_json, validation_failed, missing_target, invalid_webhook_url — malformed request.
docs.e404: 404 · webhook_not_found — unknown id, or it belongs to someone else.
docs.e422: 422 · webhook_invalid — this webhook was marked invalid by Discord.
docs.e409: 409 · duplicate_failed — idempotencyKey was already used for a failed send.
docs.e429: 429 · rate_limited — slow down (5 req/min per key).
docs.e502: 502 · discord_rate_limited, discord_error — Discord rejected the send; the attempt is logged and logId is included.
docs.rateBody: 5 requests per minute per API key — deliberately stricter than the dashboard. Exceeding it returns HTTP 429. Discord's own rate limits still apply on top of this.
docs.s1: Treat keys like passwords. The full key is displayed once and never again.
docs.s2: Only SHA-256 hashes are stored — a database leak cannot be turned back into usable keys.
docs.s3: Keys are never written to logs; only the key id and prefix appear there.
docs.s4: Give each integration its own key with an expiry date, so a leak has a blast radius of one.
docs.s5: A key can only send through your own webhooks — it cannot read or change anything else.
